subtopic: Pod Lifecycle, Liveness, Readiness and Startup Probes
question_text: [Containerization & Image Optimization (Docker) - Q47] What is the functional difference between a Kubernetes `livenessProbe` and a `readinessProbe`?

options.text: Liveness probe removes the Pod from Service endpoints; readiness probe kills and restarts the Pod
Liveness probe determines if the container needs to be killed and restarted; readiness probe determines if the container is ready to receive network traffic via Service endpoints
Readiness probe only runs during cluster bootstrap
They execute the exact same actions upon failure

answer_explanation: If a readiness probe fails, the Pod is removed from Service endpoint load balancers without restarting. If a liveness probe fails, kubelet kills the container and initiates restart policies.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: If a readiness probe fails, the Pod is removed from Service endpoint load balancers without restarting. If a liveness probe fails, kubelet kills the container and initiates restart policies.

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Selects the exact correct technical option.
